To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
communities of practice are an effective way to improve boys’ education, that there is a need for a national approach to boys’ education and that the BELS Project provides a model for this approach.

the Boys’ Education Lighhouse Project has enabled clusters of Australian schools to initiate, research and report on initiatives aimed at improving boys’ learning outcomes; clusters have focused on initiating literacy programs, modifying teacher practice, introducing male models or using ICT; and clusters show differing levels of engagement, imagination and alignement as communities of practice.

The four clusters of schools involved in the BELS Project are at varying stages of development as communities; the BELS Project is a useful framework for the development of a community of practice; and that the BELS Project provides an opportunity for the development of knowledge building in schools through a community of practice.

the development of a national community of practice in boys’ education, and the role of the BELS project in facilitating this.
